title_en: Li Jian'an, Zhang Yongdong, Wang Huili, Wang Qinghai — case of speculation and profiteering
keywords_en: criminal; speculation; second instance; High People's Court; Tianjin; natural person; criminal law; whether illegal publications constitute speculation; determination of principal and accessory offenders; determination of recidivism; affirm the original judgment; publishing illegal publications; printing and selling; seeking exorbitant profits; intentional injury; rape
full_text_en:
Li Jian'an, Zhang Yongdong, Wang Huili, and Wang Qinghai — case of speculation

Defendant Li Jian'an, male, 29 years old, formerly a worker of the Fifth Construction Team of Tianjin Fifth Municipal Engineering Company. In December 1978, he was subjected to compulsory labor for two years due to hooliganism.

Defendant Zhang Yongdong, male, 30 years old, unemployed. In May 1984, he was sentenced to one year of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of intentional injury.

Defendant Wang Huili, male, 40 years old, formerly the factory manager of the Printing Factory of Xiaowangzhuang Seventh Team, Chenzui Township, Wuqing County, Tianjin.

Defendant Wang Qinghai, male, 49 years old, formerly a business clerk of the Printing Factory of Xiaowangzhuang Seventh Team, Chenzui Township, Wuqing County, Tianjin.

All of the above defendants were arrested on July 25, 1987.

Defendants Li Jian'an, Zhang Yongdong, Wang Huili, and Wang Qinghai were prosecuted by the Tianjin Branch of the People's Procuratorate before the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court for the crime of speculation. After accepting the case, the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court conducted a public trial and found the following facts:

In September 1985, Defendants Li Jian'an and Zhang Yongdong became acquainted while trafficking in illegal publications. In June 1986, Li Jian'an observed that the illegal publication "Thought-Provoking Cases" transported to Tianjin from other places sold quickly, and suggested to Zhang Yongdong that they select "cases" similar to that publication, have them printed, and sell them for profit. Zhang Yongdong agreed. Subsequently, Li Jian'an contacted Defendants Wang Qinghai and Wang Huili through another person for printing. Wang Qinghai and Wang Huili, knowing that what Li Jian'an wanted to print was illegal publications, nevertheless agreed to undertake the printing for profit. In July, Wang Qinghai and Wang Huili further agreed with Li Jian'an and Zhang Yongdong: Li Jian'an would provide the manuscripts, and Wang Qinghai and Wang Huili would be responsible for printing and binding, at a printing cost of RMB 0.11 per copy. Wang Huili also stated that if the printing was discovered, the factory would bear the losses. Thereafter, Li Jian'an selected cases involving content such as murder, rape, and incest from over ten types of publications including "Extraordinary Cases and Detection," labeled them with violent and pornographic titles, compiled them into six volumes, still titled "Thought-Provoking Cases," forged the editorial unit — the Case Report Editorial Department, used an illegal "Guangxi Publication Registration Certificate No. 104," and handed them over to Wang Qinghai and Wang Huili for printing. Wang Qinghai and Wang Huili printed 386,364 copies for Li Jian'an; they also arranged for 253,000 copies to be printed by Huafeng Printing Factory in the same village and Fengyuan Printing Factory in Shigezhuang Township of the same county, totaling 639,364 copies. Wang Qinghai and Wang Huili profited RMB 9,770.38. Li Jian'an and Zhang Yongdong sold 525,364 copies to Tianjin, Beijing, Tangshan, Qinhuangdao, Shenyang, and other places, illegally profiting RMB 40,146.84; the remaining 114,000 copies were seized and destroyed by the public security authorities. In October of the same year, Wang Huili and Wang Qinghai printed another 380,000 copies of "Thought-Provoking Cases" for Li Jian'an and Zhang Yongdong, which were sealed and destroyed during the binding process.

The Tianjin Intermediate People's Court, after trial, held: The Defendants Li Jian'an, Zhang Yongdong, Wang Huili, and Wang Qinghai jointly committed the criminal act, constituting joint intentional crime under Article 22, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the PRC. Li Jian'an first proposed and personally compiled the "cases," arranged for printing, and conducted sales; Zhang Yongdong actively cooperated with Li Jian'an in publishing illegal publications and engaged in wholesale sales. Pursuant to Article 23, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, Li Jian'an and Zhang Yongdong were the principal offenders in this case and should be severely punished. Wang Huili and Wang Qinghai, knowing that Li Jian'an and Zhang Yongdong were publishing illegal publications, nevertheless printed them in large quantities for profit; pursuant to Article 24, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Criminal Law, they were accessories in this case and should be given lighter punishments compared to the principal offenders. Zhang Yongdong was sentenced to one year of fixed-term imprisonment for intentional injury in May 1984; within three years after the completion of his sentence, he committed another crime punishable by fixed-term imprisonment or heavier punishment, constituting a recidivist under Article 61, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, and should be given a heavier punishment. China's relevant administrative regulations clearly stipulate that the publication, production, and distribution of various publications are uniformly managed by the state; without approval from the relevant state authorities, no unit or individual may擅自 publish, produce, or distribute publications. Li Jian'an and Zhang Yongdong, without approval from the competent state authorities, for the purpose of profit, in violation of industrial and commercial administrative regulations, produced and sold in large quantities illegal publications filled with content of murder, rape, and incest, infringing upon the state's management of industry and commerce (including publishing and printing industries) and seriously disrupting the book market. Wang Huili and Wang Qinghai, knowing that Li Jian'an and Zhang Yongdong were publishing illegal publications, for profit, undertook large-scale printing for them. The acts of the above defendants all constituted the crime of speculation under Article 117 of the Criminal Law. Li Jian'an and Zhang Yongdong not only speculated on a huge scale, but the illegal publications they produced, published, and sold were widely disseminated in society, poisoning the general public, especially minors, inducing crime, and causing great harm to society; they should be punished in accordance with Article 118 of the Criminal Law. Pursuant to Article 60 of the Criminal Law, the illegal gains of the criminals shall be recovered. Accordingly, on September 9, 1987, the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court sentenced Defendant Li Jian'an to seven years of fixed-term imprisonment; Defendant Zhang Yongdong to six years of fixed-term imprisonment; Defendant Wang Huili to two years of fixed-term imprisonment; and Defendant Wang Qinghai to one year of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of speculation. The illegal gains of each defendant were ordered to be recovered.

Defendant Zhang Yongdong, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to the Tianjin High People's Court on the grounds that some facts were unclear and the sentence was too severe.

The Tianjin High People's Court, after trial, held: The appellant Zhang Yongdong and the defendants at first instance Li Jian'an, Wang Huili, and Wang Qinghai, for the purpose of profit, published, printed, and sold illegal publications, reaping huge profits, with huge amounts and serious circumstances; their acts all constituted the crime of speculation. The criminal facts of appellant Zhang Yongdong in this case are clear, and the evidence is true and sufficient; Zhang Yongdong's claim that some facts found in the first instance were unclear is unfounded. The original trial, based on the criminal facts, circumstances, and the status and role of the appellant and each defendant in the joint crime, was not improper in conviction and sentencing. Zhang Yongdong's ground for appeal requesting a lighter punishment is untenable. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 136, Item 1 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, on September 23, 1987, the court ruled to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.
